standard_prerequisites.name: Lipschitz properties of subtraction and absolute value
standard_prerequisites.statement: Subtraction and absolute value on the Cauchy reals are Lipschitz for closeness, so closeness is preserved by them.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are used at source lines 1584 and 1599.

standard_prerequisites.name: Roundedness and the triangle inequality for closeness
standard_prerequisites.statement: closeness is rounded and satisfies the triangle inequality.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are used at source lines 1589-1590 and 1602.

standard_prerequisites.name: Order density of the rationals in the Cauchy reals
standard_prerequisites.statement: Between any two related rationals there is a rational strictly between them.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces theta < epsilon at source line 1598.

core_obligations: Forward direction: using the Lipschitz properties, reduce from u close-epsilon v to the case v = 0, so that it suffices to show that u close-epsilon 0 implies |u| < eps (source lines 1584-1585).

Prove that by induction on u: the rational case is immediate, and in the limit case use roundedness to get theta with lim(x) close-(eps - theta) 0, then the triangle inequality and the inductive hypothesis to get |x_{theta/3}| < eps - 2theta/3, and finally the Lipschitz property together with the retained openness lemma to obtain |lim(x)| < eps (source lines 1586-1591).
Backward direction: induct on u and v; if both are rational it is the first constructor of closeness (source lines 1593-1594).

Mixed rational-limit case: after the inductive hypothesis, use order density to pick theta < eps, then the Lipschitz property and the retained openness lemma to get |q - y_delta| < theta + 2delta, apply the inductive hypothesis to obtain q close-(theta + 2delta) y_delta and the triangle inequality to reach q close-(theta + 4delta) lim(y), and choose delta := (eps - theta)/4 (source lines 1596-1603).
Record that the remaining two cases are entirely analogous (source line 1605).

proof_roadmap.step: Forward direction reduced to v = 0 and proved by induction.
Backward direction, mixed case with the choice of delta; the other cases are analogous.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 11.3.44 at source lines 1578-1582: closeness coincides with the distance inequality |u - v| < eps. The author's proof (source lines 1583-1606) is a two-direction induction whose non-trivial cases are quantitative: the forward direction is reduced to the case v = 0 by the Lipschitz properties (line 1584), and its limit case combines roundedness, the triangle inequality, the inductive hypothesis and the retained openness lemma before the Lipschitz property closes the estimate (lines 1586-1591); the backward direction treats rational-rational by a constructor (line 1594) and then the mixed case, where order density produces theta < eps, the Lipschitz property and the retained openness lemma give |q - y_delta| < theta + 2delta, the inductive hypothesis gives q close-(theta + 2delta) y_delta, and the triangle inequality plus the choice delta := (eps - theta)/4 finishes (lines 1596-1603); the remaining two cases are declared analogous (line 1605). The statement is a bare equivalence of relations and records none of the estimates.
